entries.title: How Gemini is changing the game for Golden State's organization and fans.
entries.summary: Google Gemini partners with Golden State to power fan experiences and business operations for the Warriors, Valkyries, and Chase Center. See the news.
entries.content:
Today, we’re expanding our partnership with Golden State — making Google Gemini the Official AI Assistant Partner and Official Generative AI & Enterprise LLM Partner of the Warriors, the 2026 WNBA Champion Valkyries, and Chase Center.

The collaboration integrates Gemini across the entire franchise ecosystem. For fans, that means a more interactive game-day experience, both inside Chase Center via interactive videoboard features, and across digital channels for fans following from home. And behind the scenes, Golden State is deploying Gemini for business to build custom AI agents, helping their teams work smarter across both business and basketball operations.

As a Founding Partner of Chase Center since 2019, Golden State has used our gen AI tools to help their operations run smoother, and this next chapter brings the best of Gemini to the team and fans alike.

entries.title: Independent filmmakers in India bring big-screen stories to life with Google Flow.
entries.summary: Indian filmmakers use Google Flow to create original short films. Watch five winning stories from the WIF India Filmathon. See the films now.
entries.content:
Every culture has its own visual language, and new tools are helping more storytellers share theirs with the world. We partnered with Women in Film India (WIF India) to launch the WIF India × Google Flow Filmathon, designed to democratize AI filmmaking and elevate talent beyond traditional production centers across India.

Using Google Flow, our AI creative studio, participants paired their creative visions with AI to build original worlds from scratch. Five finalist short films recently debuted at the International Film Festival of India in Goa, bringing fresh, creative voices from across the country to the festival screen. The winners received their awards from the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Goa Dr. Pramod Sawant.

Click through the carousel below to watch all five short films made with Google Flow and experience a bold new wave of independent storytelling.

entries.title: We’re expanding our London home in King's Cross.
entries.summary: Sticky Note Art in 6 Pancras Square
entries.content:
In 2016, we arrived in King’s Cross as founding residents of the Knowledge Quarter. Today, we’re announcing our plan to purchase 6 Pancras Square.

Alongside Central Saint Giles and Platform 37, this investment cements our London campus as a key AI development hub. These offices will be home to thousands of Googlers who help build products like Gemini, Search and YouTube, which contribute £140bn to the UK’s economy.

Incredible ideas happen when people connect, whether co-creating in our Accessibility Discovery Centre, launching Fuel Prices on Google Maps, or researching how AI can improve breast cancer detection.

Our campus will continue to bolster community and innovation. Alongside our £5bn investment in the UK, including our Waltham Cross data centre, AI Campus, the forthcoming AI Exchange, as well as our decade long upskilling programme that has trained over 1.2 million Brits, we’re investing in the people, places, and partnerships shaping Britain’s future growth.

entries.title: See what 6 builders are making with Gemini 4 Hydrogen
entries.summary: Collage of six 3D graphics showcasing virtual environments, interactive scenes, and model comparisons including "Gemini 4 Hydrogen" and "Gemini 3.8 Flash."
entries.content:
We recently introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, bringing cutting-edge intelligence to everyone. Built for rapid execution across diverse agentic workflows, Hydrogen can stand on its own as a model for everyday work — or pair with Carbon as the high-efficiency execution engine in multi-model workflows. Thanks to these capabilities, builders have already been putting Hydrogen to work. Check out six projects showing what Hydrogen can do.

Code a sci-fi journey through rainy skies.

@kimmonismus created a sci-fi-inspired journey through a Three.js skyline with Hydrogen on high thinking in Google Antigravity.

Fly a seaplane from morning to night.

@LuminaBench swept across the sea by plane, showing the passage of time as the scene changes from morning to night.

Build a blocky koi pond.

@IamEmily2050 used Hydrogen in the Gemini app to create a 3D voxel koi pond, complete with a red pagoda, cherry blossoms, and lantern-lit bridges.

Create a jelly-like koi pond instead.

Speaking of koi ponds, @notjazii used Hydrogen to put a softer spin on a koi pond with a squishy, jelly-like form instead of angular edges.

Animate an interactive ruby-red moth.

@thtbee_ brought a crimson moth to life pairing our two latest models in Google Antigravity. Gemini 4 Carbon orchestrated a /swarm of Hydrogen workers to create an interactive animation with atmospheric visuals and sound. Then Hydrogen recorded the demo video, too.

Compare a 3D desert ranch across Gemini models.

And @Bhavani_00007 gave us a look at the progression from Gemini 3.8 Flash to Hydrogen by running the same animated 3D desert ranch prompt on both, with Hydrogen bringing the scene to life in <1 minute.

Developers can get started with Gemini 4 Hydrogen using the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Android Studio, and paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can try it in Google Antigravity. Anyone can use Hydrogen in the Gemini app drop down 1 and Google Search, and enterprise teams can access it in Gemini for business.

entries.title: Here are 4 things you didn’t know you could do with Gemini Canvas.
entries.summary: Boost productivity with Google Gemini Canvas. Build web apps, create custom study tools, and refine writing side-by-side. Try it in your next chat.
entries.content:
Gemini Canvas gives you an interactive workspace alongside your chat. Here are four ways to use it.

  • Create web apps and mini-games: Build 3D visualizers, playable browser games, and more.
  • Make custom study tools: Turn notes or PDFs into interactive quizzes, flashcards, and sandboxes.
  • Design office productivity boosters: Convert spreadsheets into sales trackers, pricing calculators, and task lists.
  • Refine writing side-by-side: Highlight text directly on the canvas to adjust tone, rephrase sections, or restructure proposals.

Try it in your next chat.

entries.title: A more tailored Google Search that’s uniquely yours
entries.summary: Google Search bar with the text "Personal Intelligence" surrounded by the Google Wallet, Google Drive, GMail, Google Photos, Google Calendar, and Google G logo icons
entries.content:
The most helpful search experience brings together the richness of the world’s information with insights uniquely relevant to you. Today, Search is getting even more tailored with the ability to connect more of your apps to Personal Intelligence — and we're introducing more personally relevant responses, so it's easier to find just what you need.

Starting to roll out today, you can opt in to securely connect Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, with support for Drive and the Gemini app following in the coming weeks — bringing context from your spending, documents, and chats directly to Search. These apps join Gmail, Calendar, and Photos in delivering even more tailored responses with your personal context.

  • Get a clearer picture of your spending with Google Wallet: By connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence in both AI Mode and the Gemini app, you can map out your financial milestones and identify actionable ways to trim everyday spending. You can also maximize credit card benefits — like optimizing cash-back categories, travel perks, and reward points — based on your cards linked via Wallet. If you choose to connect your Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from your accounts; it can’t move, manage, or invest your money.
  • Stay in your flow with Google Drive: Sometimes the important information that you need to get started on a project or make a big decision can be scattered across your docs, sheets, or PDFs. With Google Drive connected in Personal Intelligence, you can get uniquely helpful responses that take all of that context into account and help you get started, like a personalized preparation plan ahead of tax season.
  • Connect the dots between the Gemini app and Search: In the coming weeks you can easily share context across the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search. So if you explore an idea in the Gemini app, AI Mode will have that foundation to build on, and vice versa. While you could already opt in to connect your Search history to Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app, soon you can also opt in to securely connect your Gemini app to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode.

To connect your apps to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, open Search Personalization, select Connected Apps, and then choose the apps you want to connect. You choose if and when you opt in, and you can turn those connections on or off at any time. You’re always in control of your personalization settings, and soon you’ll also be able to view the context AI Mode uses via the “Personalization” icon below any tailored response. If you want to edit anything simply let AI Mode know what to change, like responding in thread “I’m no longer a vegetarian.”

You’ll also start seeing more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode, tailored to your recent search context. So if you’ve been researching and planning for a trip, you can pick up right where you left off in a new search thread without starting over or repeating yourself. As always, you can adjust or turn off personalization at any time in your Search Settings.

entries.title: Organize and share your holiday memories with these five updates in Google Photos.
entries.summary: Organize holiday memories with five new Google Photos updates. Use Gemini for video tasks and filter shared albums by people. Try these features today.
entries.content:
From Thanksgiving feasts to family reunions, here’s how recent Google Photos updates help you spend less time managing memories and more time making them:

  1. Make a highlight album of our Thanksgiving celebration, email the link to my family, and include a quick recap of the day.
  2. Turn festive memories into scrapbook-style holiday cards or pastel illustrations with 12 new Remix templates.
  3. Filter shared albums by people or pets so you don’t have to scroll to find what you need. Tap any face in the top carousel to instantly see photos of yourself, loved ones, or pets.
  4. Customize your Collections tab by pinning your favorite albums and memories front and center, and hiding what you don't use. On Android, you can easily access local media with "On this device."
  5. Create personalized gifts like photo books, blankets, mugs, and more through the Fujifilm for Google Photos Print Store.

Try these updates in Google Photos today and celebrate what matters most.

entries.title: Introducing file slicing controls in the Gemini API
entries.content:
Today, we're launching new file slicing controls in the API across Google AI Studio and Gemini platform, alongside native file upload support for Microsoft Office and OpenDocument formats. You can now pass PDFs, Office files (docs, slides, spreadsheets), audio, and video directly to the Gemini API and request only the pages, spreadsheet cells, media segments, and layers you need. This keeps context focused on the relevant parts of a file while billing tokens only for the parts Gemini inspects.

Inspect only what you need

Real-world knowledge work lives in dense PDFs, slide decks, multi-tab workbooks, and long recordings. With server-side slicing, you do not have to flatten files to plain text or ingest entire files up front.

  • Upload once, slice across turns: Upload a file once with the Files API and reuse its URI across turns and tool calls.
  • Give your agent control: The API lets the agent specify what parts of a file to inspect directly inside a function response for faster and more efficient multi-turn workflows
  • Skim cheap, then zoom in: Skim first with extracted text, low-res previews, or transcripts, then spend high-resolution tokens only on the charts, dense layouts, and frames that matter.

Slice documents, spreadsheets, and videos and more by range, layer, resolution, and frame rate to control token usage.

Make your harness multimodal without local bloat

When model APIs only ingest whole files, agents end up running LibreOffice, PDF renderers, and 

ffmpeg
inside the client harness to render and slice large files. This bloats memory, clutters local disk with extracted frames, and forces enterprise platforms to maintain per-user sandboxes just to slice files. With the Gemini API, pass a Files API URI on a user turn or directly inside a function response (
function_result
), and the API natively slices, renders, and tokenizes each file server-side the way the model was trained to see it.

How it works

Native file slicing works across all Gemini 4 models, and existing file size and page limits still apply to the uploaded file. You can customize processing across these media categories:

  • Documents and slides (PDF, Office and OpenDocument formats): Select a page range (start_page, end_page), set resolution (low, medium, or high), and choose content layers (page_text or page_image).
  • Spreadsheets (.xlsx, .xls, .ods): Select a worksheet tab (sheet_index) and cell range (visible_cells), set resolution (low, medium, or high), and select content layers (data, formulas, and visuals).
  • Video: Clip time intervals (start_offset, end_offset), adjust fps and resolution (low, high), and choose content layers (transcript, frames, or audio).
  • Audio: clip time intervals (start_offset, end_offset) with ease.

When processing options are omitted from API calls, documents and slides default to layout-preserving page images, and spreadsheets include evaluated values, formulas, and sheet names across all tabs.

Example: Skim at a high level, zoom in on details

Upload a Word document once to the Files API, skim every page cheaply as extracted text to locate the right section, then reuse the same URI to inspect a single page at high resolution:

from google import genai


client = genai.Client()
doc = client.files.upload(file="quarterly_report.docx")


# 1. Skim the whole document cheaply as extracted text.
skim = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
    input=[
        {
            "type": "document",
            "uri": doc.uri,
            "mime_type": doc.mime_type,
            "processing": {
                "type": "static",
                "page_options": {"content_layers": ["page_text"]},
            },
        },
        {
            "type": "text",
            "text": "Which page has the revenue bridge chart?",
        },
    ],
)
print(skim.output_text)


# 2. Zoom into the target page at high resolution (reusing the same URI).
detail = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    input=[
        {
            "type": "document",
            "uri": doc.uri,
            "mime_type": doc.mime_type,
            "resolution": "high",
            "processing": {
                "type": "static",
                "page_options": {
                    "start_page": 3,
                    "end_page": 3,
                    "content_layers": ["page_image"],
                },
            },
        },
        {
            "type": "text",
            "text": "Read the revenue bridge chart and footnotes on page 3.",
        },
    ],
)
print(detail.output_text)

Early adoption across agent frameworks

Gateway and SDK partners validated these controls ahead of launch, cutting prompt token spend directly in production harnesses:

Get started

Native file slicing, content-layer controls, and expanded files support are available today via the API in Google AI Studio and the Gemini platform. Check out our docs to start building.

entries.title: Get your year-end tasks done with new Connected Apps.
entries.summary: Google Connected Apps simplify your year-end tasks. Manage groceries, credit scores, and home services directly in Search. Get the details for November 2026.
entries.content:
Tackling your to-do list just got a little easier. In the U.S., we’re rolling out new Connected Apps through Search and the Gemini app to help with your grocery runs, including Albertsons, Safeway, Shaw’s, and Target.

Whether you’re preparing appetizers for your holiday party or need groceries for Thanksgiving, these new Connected Apps can help you build your order and check out with ease. Powered by the Universal Commerce Protocol, these apps can help you get more done this holiday season.

The end of the year is also a great time to get your finances in order. Experian is already live on the Gemini app, and now we’re rolling it out to Search with the ability to help U.S. users check their credit rating and shop for a personal loan. U.S. users can also turn to H&R Block to calculate their taxes and estimate their refunds right from Search.

In the coming weeks, you’ll also be able to link your accounts to Angi and Thumbtack in Search, streamlining your hunt for local pros who can fix that leaky faucet or put up last-minute decorations before your guests arrive.

entries.title: How Watch Duty is using Gemini to get wildfire alerts out faster
entries.content:
This July, as the Railroad Fire spread through Washington overnight, Watch Duty sent its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert to its users. It started with a 911 dispatch buried in radio static — and a new Gemini tool that caught it in seconds.

A dedicated team of Google engineers and researchers spent six months embedded full-time with Watch Duty, a nonprofit wildfire alert app run by active and retired firefighters, dispatchers, and first responders. Through the Google.org Fellowship, they used more than 20,000 hours of past radio recordings to build a Gemini-powered tool that wipes out heavy static and translates specialized firefighting terminology into clean, searchable text. The system removes the added strain of deciphering noisy audio so volunteers can focus on verifying incidents and getting alerts out.

The challenge

When a wildfire starts, minutes can decide whether people get out safely. Yet across much of the country, the first word of a new fire still travels over decades-old analog VHF radio, where engine noise, wind, static, and rapid-fire tactical jargon make it hard to hear what's happening. Watch Duty reporters monitor up to 20 feeds manually, making it a challenge to cut through the noise.

The results

Across Watch Duty's network, the tool has:

  • Helped close coverage gaps in areas with no other automated dispatch detection, sending reporters a signal in less than 30 seconds; this way, a new fire isn't missed just because no one was listening at that moment
  • Reduced word error rate on degraded VHF radio audio from 38% down to 22.34%
  • Transcribed more than 200 hours of radio speech a day from about 400 active feeds, and has been designed and tested to handle more than 10,000 feeds at once.

As a result of the collaboration between Google and Watch Duty, volunteer reporter satisfaction with radio transcription tools increased from 35.3% to 92.3%.

The tool was also put to test during a live fire. In July 2026, a fast-moving wildfire — the Railroad Fire — ignited at night in Washington. When the first 911 dispatch went out over local fire radio, the Gemini-powered transcription tool transcribed it straight from the noisy radio audio and flagged it in under 30 seconds.

That head start gave Watch Duty's team the time they needed to verify the fire and push a Critical Alert—which breaks through do-not-disturb mode in urgent situations—helping residents evacuate before flames reached homes. It was the first time Watch Duty had ever sent a Critical Alert overnight, proving what faster detection means when communities are asleep and every minute counts.

The collaboration

The new AI radio tool is the latest milestone in a deep, multi-year collaboration spanning Google's philanthropic, product, and research teams to help Watch Duty scale its life-saving mission across all 50 states.

  • Funding: In 2024, Google.org provided Watch Duty with $2 million in funding and $300,000 in Google Cloud credits to help compile satellite, camera, and radio data to validate new fires.
  • Search: During US fires such as the Palisades, Eaton, Hurst, and Auto fires, Google Search featured Watch Duty in SOS alerts alongside official emergency guidance.
  • Alerts at scale: Watch Duty sends push alerts through Firebase Cloud Messaging. As its audience grew to more than 16 million people last year, Google Cloud raised its messaging limit from 600,000 to 1 million to help alerts arrive without delay.
  • Broader industry partnership: As part of the AI Collaborative: Wildfires, Watch Duty is turning models and data into tools that agencies, communities, and responders trust and use.

When the next fire starts, the goal is simple: get people the warning they need while there's still time to act.
